item.title: SQL Query to Fetch Latest Record Per Group Using Window Functions vs Aggregation
item.description:
“SQL Query to Fetch Latest Record Per Group Using Window Functions vs Aggregation”

When dealing with time-stamped transactional data, a frequent requirement is isolating the single, most recent record associated with each unique entity or ID. How can this be achieved efficiently in a relational database like Oracle, especially when the dataset contains multiple entries for the same ID, differentiated by a timestamp? We will explore two robust methodologies: leveraging modern window functions and employing traditional aggregate joins.

item.title: SQL: Retrieving Max Round and Corresponding Score Per ID Without Subqueries
item.description:
“SQL: Retrieving Max Round and Corresponding Score Per ID Without Subqueries”

When working with relational data, particularly in tables like SCORES which track sequential events (represented by round) for entities (represented by id), a frequent requirement is to retrieve the entire row, or specific columns, corresponding to the highest value in one column (e.g., round) for each group (e.g., id). How can we achieve this specific retrieval effectively, perhaps avoiding explicit subqueries or common table expressions (CTEs) for performance or stylistic reasons?
